findings.fact: SEC Grant conflicting with the Runtime Identity enrolled Intent selected Grant must hard deny skill_context_grant_conflict; do not loosen this to make two Skills pass.
Public flow exists: import -> permission draft -> approve -> install plan -> apply -> activate -> runtime identity -> enrolled session -> admin-issued SEC.
Runtime snapshot explicitly requires the current project siq_analysis source; cannot substitute an unrelated profile and call it the same business entry.

implementation_requirements: Use one owned discovered Agent with two actual installed Skills; record real source and installed content digests.
Select the matching installed Skill Grant for each runtime identity and matching SEC; same Agent may have distinct bounded identities/tasks.
Bind actual loaded Skill bytes in the OpenShell runtime to the recorded installation; a host-only installation plus a claimed Skill name is insufficient.
Trusted host/controller may approve and issue contexts; model and sandbox must not receive admin/recovery credentials or approval authority.
If a test-only synchronization hook is needed to expose native session/task identity, label it and verify unmodified product decisions and real tool dispatch separately.
Negative controls: unapproved import, Skill A identity with Skill B SEC, revoked context, content drift, out-of-scope write; include normal read/write controls.
user_authorization: Directly repair and optimize discovered issues; claims require observed evidence, not merely target outcome.
